title: Weekly (Sun) I-91 Overpass Standout - 9 Mtn Park Rd, Holyoke, MA
description:
Trying a Sunday standout again, for those who can't make our weekday afternoons. It's a kid-friendly space on a lightly traveled roadway. Let's make this thing GROW!!!

Come out to show that ordinary people can raise their voices against the chaos and destruction of this Administration. Help remind folks that they, too, can stand up for their beliefs - and that there's lots and lots of people who aren't on board with the "cruelty as entertainment" behavior of Trump and Musk and the GOP.

### Recent DOT Visits

A Department of Transportation employee has visited twice in the past three weeks prior to 5/20 to ask that people NOT attach anything to the fencing. On 5/20, he parked and waited until everything was removed from the fencing. It seems reasonable to expect that DOT enforcement will continue.

### How to Get There

The address "9 Mountain Park Rd, Holyoke" will get you there if you're using Waze. (Mountain Park Road runs off Route 5, and is not accessible from I-91.) People have reported that some GPS systems bring you right under the bridge, but on I-91. That’s annoying!

Please park on the side of the road before the bridge. We can't park on the bridge.

### Other Stuff

Please take everything you brought away with you, and leave the site totally clean.

If rain is predicted, we'll cancel. If we cancel, you'll receive an email notification.

We may see a counter protester. If so, the best thing to do is just ignore them and spend our time and energy waving to motorists. Let's keep things 100% non-confrontational in words and body language.

### A Few Requests

We've found that roof rake sections make wonderful flagpoles and banner poles. If you have a roof rake (or 10’-15’ light metal poles or conduit) to contribute, we'll be happy to take it off your hands!

Donations...we've purchased banners and grommets and flags and zip ties and bungee cords, and we'll be getting more. We’ve purchased 20” x 30” letter boards for messaging we can change. All this costs $$$. We'll have a bucket for donations, and if you could throw something in, that'd be great. And if not, that's perfectly OK, too - your presence is what's really important. See where the money's going! https://tinyurl.com/IN-SLWMProtestTeamFinancials

description:
At our Compost Hubs, food scraps collected from the community are transformed into nutrient-rich compost, and we need your help to make it happen! As a Compost Hub Support Volunteer, you’ll gain hands-on experience working alongside our knowledgeable Compost Managers. Get ready to leave feeling accomplished, a little sweaty, and brimming with new compost knowledge. 

#### ABOUT ACTIVITY:
Roll up your sleeves and dive into a variety of engaging activities like reactivating the worm bin with coco coir and sifting through compost. Join passionate community composters, learn to turn food scraps into rich compost. 

#### MORE INFO: 
* You will be working outdoors! Shade levels vary by site.
* Activities level can be adjusted to your comfort and abilities—just communicate with your Compost Manager.
* No prior composting experience is needed; everyone is welcome!
* This location has bathrooms available
* If you sign up, we ask that you show up! We rely on volunteers, like you, to achieve our mission.  
* We’ll follow up with details via email, so be sure to provide your best contact email when signing up.

#### SUMMER ACCOMMODATIONS:
Don’t forget that we are in full swing of summer at LA Compost, and we want to ensure that all our volunteers are comfortable and well taken care of during their time with us. 

Here are some accommodations we have in place:

* Ice Water Provided: To help you stay hydrated in the summer heat, we will have ice-cold water available at all our sites. Please feel free to bring your reusable water bottles to stay eco-friendly!
* Regular Breaks: We understand the importance of rest, especially in warmer weather. Regular breaks will ensure you can relax and recharge in shady areas.
* Shady Activities: We will prioritize activities in the shade as much as possible to keep everyone cool and comfortable.

#### AGE REQUIREMENT:
This volunteer activity is best suited for volunteers aged 16 and up. Minors under the age of 16 should come accompanied by a parent or guardian unless other arrangements are made. Contact ashleigh@lacompost.org for more information.

Please make sure you have signed the volunteer waiver.

Meeting Point: De Vargas Park (a few blocks from the El Dorado Hotel)
What: Peaceful rally and march to the El Dorado Hotel (WGA meeting location)

We need you there: Plan to bring friends, family, and anyone who cares about our public lands. Come with signs supporting public lands and national monuments. We need to organize a HUGE turnout for this peaceful rally and march. Please share far and wide!



As New Mexicans, we love our public lands and believe they belong in public hands. Our shared love for these special places unites us. Let's come together to make sure these leaders hear that message loud and clear!

description:

Join Armstrong for All in canvassing the West Seattle Farmers Market!

Sign up here to be counted in, and we'll help get you trained so you can do this democracy thing with confidence.

Meet at 9:45 for a quick training, and the farmers market runs from 10 AM - 2 PM.

About Ry: Ry is a queer elected labor leader and climate organizer running to lower the costs of living in Seattle, and will fight for every-day families. As a Millennial in their 30s who was raised in a Seattle union family, Ry knows that Seattle is at its best when it is sustainable, labor strong, and just. In order to achieve this vision, Seattle needs and deserves a leader who will act with honesty, transparency, and follow through to deliver on promises, which has not happened under the current administration. Ry has the professional talent, conviction, and moral compass to serve the City of Seattle, and welcomes you to be part of this pivotal moment in Seattle history.
